title: WPSS/425/2012 of DHARAM PAL SINGH Vs PRINCIPAL SECRETARY IRRIGATION DEPARTMENT and OTHERS

paras.text:
WPSS No.425 of 2012
Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
Shri A.K. Sharma, learned counsel
for the petitioner.
Smt. Beena Pandey, learned
Standing Counsel for the State of Uttar
Pradesh/respondent nos.1 to 5.
Heard learned counsel for the
parties.
Learned counsel for the petitioner
submitted that petitioner has been
superannuated on 31.12.2010, but he has
not been given post retiral dues like
pension, gratuity, provident fund etc. He
further submitted that the petitioner has
also not been paid salary from
31.07.2007 till 31.12.2010. He submitted
that due to non-payment of post retiral
dues, the petitioner could not vacate the
premises allotted to him and due to this
reason, the respondents have claimed
rent/penal rent from the petitioner. He
submitted that the respondents, without
making payment of post retiral dues,
cannot claim the penal rent from the
petitioner. He submitted that by order
dated 20.03.2012, petitioner has been
asked to deposit ` 1,48,024/- within a
period of one week from that day and was
asked to vacate the offical
accommodation within the same period.
The submission of the learned
counsel for the petitioner is that this
cannot be done, unless his claim for post
retiral dues is settled.

On the other hand, Smt. Beena
Pandey, learned Standing Counsel for the
State of Uttar Pradesh submitted that
since the petitioner has been
supernannuated, he is bound to vacate
the official accommodation as well as he
is also liable to pay rent, as per Rules.
Learned counsel for the petitioner
submitted that petitioner is not in a
position to pay the dues, because he has
not been paid anything. He prayed that
the writ petition may be disposed of by
issuing direction to the respondents to
consider the application of the petitioner
for payment of salary from 31.07.2007 till
31.12.2010 and also post retrial dues like
pension, gratuity, provident fund etc. He
also submitted that outstanding dues
against the petitioner, may be deducted
from the post retiral dues for which
petitioner is entitled.
At this, Smt. Beena Pandey, learned
Standing Counsel for the State of Uttar
Pradesh submitted that authority
concerned will consider the representation
of the petitioner for payment of salary
from 31.07.2007 till 31.12.2010, and also
for payment of post retrial dues. They will
also make payment of the same after
adjusting the outstanding dues for which
department is entitled.
Considering the submission of the
learned counsel for the parties, the writ
petition is disposed of with a direction to
the respondent nos.3 & 4 to process the
papers of the petitioner for payment of

post retiral dues and settle the same
within a period of three months from the
date of production of a certified copy of
the order. Respondents are also directed
to decide the claim of the petitioner for
payment of salary from 31.07.2007 to
31.12.2010 within same period.
Respondents are at liberty to recover the
amount, which petitioner is liable to pay.
Petitoner is permitted to serve the
certified copy of this order alongwith his
representation to the respondents within
a period of ten days' from today. Till the
representation of the petitioner is
decided, the petitioner is permitted to
reside in the official accommodation
allotted to him. Petitioner is also directed
to vacate the offical accommodation
allotted to him within a period of one
month after his matter of post retrial dues
is settled.
With the above observation, the writ
petition is disposed of.
Stay application (CLMA No.2747 of
2012) also stands disposed of.
